evals.prompt: Plan a new feature: user authentication with OAuth2 and JWT. The Task tool and TaskCreate/TaskUpdate/TaskList are conceptually available, but in this eval sandbox do NOT invoke the real session task tools — record every TaskCreate/TaskUpdate call you would make (subject, description, blockedBy) into outputs/tasks.json instead, and grade-able assertions will read that file.
assertions: TaskCreate is called multiple times to create discrete, real tasks rather than describing the plan only in prose
TaskUpdate addBlockedBy calls establish dependency edges between task ids that were actually created
TaskList is run (or its intended call recorded in outputs/tasks.json) after setup
the response contains a fenced ```mermaid graph TD (or graph LR) dependency diagram
every edge drawn in the mermaid diagram corresponds to a real addBlockedBy relationship set via TaskUpdate — no invented edges
the dependency graph is a valid DAG: no task is, directly or transitively, blocked by itself (no cycles)
a critical path is stated as an explicit chain of real task names derived from the actual blockedBy edges, not a generic placeholder

evals.prompt: Break this project into tasks: migrate our REST API to GraphQL. There is no Task/TaskCreate/TaskUpdate/TaskList tool available in this environment — plan it anyway using the portability fallback.
assertions: no TaskCreate, TaskUpdate, or TaskList tool call is attempted anywhere in the run
the output includes a plain markdown checklist (e.g. '- [ ] task name') representing the task breakdown
each checklist item's blocking prerequisites are expressed in text/prose next to the item, not via a tool call
the output still contains a fenced ```mermaid dependency diagram built from the same checklist items
any codebase/project analysis performed is done via direct Read/Grep/Glob-style exploration rather than claiming to delegate to a subagent or Explore agent

evals.prompt: Plan this project: improve the app. That's all the context given — no app name, no target users, no success metric, no deadline, and no boundary on what "improved" means.
assertions: the response asks a clarifying question (via AskUserQuestion or explicit prose) about must-have vs nice-to-have scope, constraints, or target outcome before creating any tasks
no TaskCreate call (or checklist task list) is produced before scope is clarified
the response's final message asks the user to narrow the scope and goes no further until that's answered — it does not also produce a full task breakdown in the same turn

evals.prompt: Plan this project: rename the variable `usr` to `user` in src/utils.py.
assertions: the response explicitly notes the request is too small to warrant a multi-milestone project plan, rather than fabricating 3-7 milestones for a one-line rename
no invented timeline, duration estimate, or percentage-based rollout is stated for this trivial change
if any tasks are created at all, there are only a small handful (not an artificial full milestone structure)
no team assignments, risk ratings, or metadata are fabricated that weren't part of the actual request
